summary: The B1 verification execution ladder is complete and closed as a passive-plus-bounded foundation: a digest-stable plan artifact (B1.1), a HITL approval bound to the exact plan digest (B1.2), a receipt contract (B1.3A), a bounded runner that executes exactly one in-code profile per invocation with fixed argv, shell=False, env allowlist, timeout, and git preflight/postflight mutation detection (B1.3B, hardened in B1.3C, broadened to a second profile docs_audit in B1.5), and a passive ledger with index/query/integrity/reconstruction reports (B1.4A-D). The gating mechanism is a two-key lock: the profile must exist in the in-code SUPPORTED_COMMAND_PROFILES table in verification_execution_runner.py (which fixes argv and timeout at code level) AND appear in the approval's approved_command_profiles/approved_step_ids, which must themselves be subsets of the plan's allowed_command_profiles/planned_steps; the plan digest and approval digest are both embedded in the receipt, and the ledger chain_digest binds plan+approval+receipt digests plus receipt_status and runner_mode. Promoting a governed "run the target repo test suite" (pytest_full) profile is architecturally straightforward (add one entrypoint + one table entry) but is blocked by concrete debt: the default plan's pytest profile violates the runner's profile==step_id==ref-leaf invariant, receipts capture no target-repo commit SHA (so they cannot serve as source-state-bound TestPassCertificate evidence), no structured test-outcome payload exists, no machine-checkable promotion-gate evaluator (B2.0 slice) exists, the ledger's optional append-chain fields are validated but never produced, and CodeVault's epistemic states have no verified tier or receipt importer.

gaps: No runnable test-suite profile: SUPPORTED_COMMAND_PROFILES in verification_execution_runner.py (lines 69-84) contains only platform_status and docs_audit; the plan's python_pytest_full and release_proof entries (verification_execution_plan.py lines 116-128) are declared but unrunnable, and verification_runner_entrypoints.py has no pytest entrypoint.

Naming invariant violation blocks the pytest lane as shipped: the default plan defines profile='python_pytest_full' with step_id='pytest_full' and ref 'verification_profiles.builder_full.pytest_full' (verification_execution_plan.py lines 116-121 and 156-162), but _validate_fixed_profile (runner lines 135-156) requires step_id==profile and command_profile_ref=='verification_profiles.builder_full.<profile>', and the approval-step check (runner lines 443-444) requires profile.step_id in approved_step_ids. With current defaults a runner profile keyed either 'python_pytest_full' or 'pytest_full' fails one of these checks, so the plan defaults must be renamed (digest-affecting change) before promotion.

Receipts carry no target-repo commit identity: _git_state (runner lines 159-189) runs only 'git status --porcelain=v1'; no HEAD SHA, branch, or tag is recorded anywhere in the receipt. A receipt therefore cannot assert 'tests passed at commit X', which is the minimum requirement for a TestPassCertificate-style promotion signal.

No structured test outcome evidence: process_results record only returncode, status (success/non_zero_exit/timeout), argv_digest, and stdout/stderr sha256+64KiB excerpts (runner lines 201-227). There are no pass/fail/skip counts, no junit-xml artifact under artifact_root, and the actual argv is not recorded (only its digest), so the argv->digest mapping is only verifiable against a specific builder-II code version, which the receipt also does not record.

No machine-checkable promotion gate (B2.0): B1_B2_RUNTIME_GOVERNANCE_COMPLETION_MAP.md line 47 names slice 'B2.0 Machine-checkable capability promotion gate/checklist'; grep across builder_ii/ finds no promotion_gate module and no CLI that consumes plan/approval/receipt/ledger digests and emits a pass/fail promotion-evidence artifact (the only 'capability_promotion_gates' code is in deepagents_execution.py, an unrelated surface).

Ledger append-chain never produced: _validate_optional_index_chain (verification_execution_ledger.py lines 498-565) validates ledger_index/previous_ledger_record_digest when present, but create_verification_execution_ledger_record (lines 759-850) never emits them, so chain_continuity_status is permanently 'not_applicable_no_sequence_rule' and the ledger has no tamper-evident ordering; ordering rests on receipt.generated_at strings.

Approval expiry not enforced: finalize_verification_execution_approval accepts expires_at (verification_execution_approval.py lines 159, 203, 352-354) but run_approved_verification in the runner never reads it (grep for expires_at in verification_execution_runner.py returns nothing), so a stale approval runs forever.

Denial evidence cannot enter the ledger: builder-ledger index-receipt (ledger_cli.py lines 254-267) and validate_receipt_chain_for_ledger (ledger 742-756) refuse chains where receipt valid!=true, and BLOCKED_BEFORE_EXECUTION receipts always set valid=false (runner line 296), so blocked/denied runs are structurally invisible to ledger-based promotion queries.

No CodeVault consumption path: code_vault/epistemic.py has no status above validation_only/hypothesis and no module in builder_ii/code_vault/ imports or references verification execution receipts, ledger records, or their digests, so receipt evidence currently cannot advance any CodeVault artifact's epistemic/promotion state.

Docs drift: ROADMAP.md line 49 and B1_CLOSURE_AUDIT.md (lines 3, 10, 19) still describe the runner as bounded to 'one approved platform_status profile', while platform_completion_audit.py and the runner itself include docs_audit (B1.5); docs/VERIFICATION_PROFILES.md documents only the passive builder-verification profile surface and neither it nor any docs/ page documents the builder-verify run-approved two-profile lane end-to-end (no docs/VERIFICATION_EXECUTION*.md exists; ls docs/ confirms).

Plan validator hard-pins target_profile=builder/verification_profile=builder_full (verification_execution_plan.py lines 282-306), so a governed test-suite run against a generic or core target repo cannot even be planned; target_repo is a free string but every command_profile_ref must begin with 'verification_profiles.builder_full.'.

risks: Mutation-detection false positives will invalidate pytest receipts: the runner treats any git porcelain change as workspace mutation (verification_execution_runner.py lines 495-525), and pytest routinely writes .pytest_cache/__pycache__/.coverage; in repos where these are not gitignored every pytest_full receipt would be FAILED/invalid. Mitigations (disable cacheprovider, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE) must not weaken the invariant into an allowlist of mutations.

Interpreter/environment mismatch for external target repos: fixed argv uses sys.executable with PYTHONPATH=target_repo and an env allowlist (runner lines 40-57, 123-132), so target-repo test suites needing their own venv/uv environment either fail to import dependencies or require forwarding more environment (contradicting B1.3C secret-stripping) or invoking uv (which writes .venv, tripping mutation detection). This is the hardest open design decision for the pytest profile.

Digest-bound approvals are brittle to plan-default changes: any edit to _default_allowed_command_profiles/_default_planned_steps (needed for the naming fix) changes plan digests and silently invalidates all existing approvals; sequencing of the naming fix, schema bumps, and commit-identity fields must be planned to avoid repeated approval churn.

Fixed 30s-per-profile timeout model does not fit test suites: timeout_policy declares operator_override_enabled=false (verification_execution_receipt.py line 91), so long suites force either very large static timeouts (weakening boundedness) or a policy change that itself needs governance review.

Approval prose scanners forbid the word 'pytest' (RAW_COMMAND_PATTERNS in verification_execution_approval.py line 53) and plan text scanners forbid 'pytest'-prefixed strings, so operators cannot describe the test lane in approval_reason; teams may either weaken the scanner (injection-surface risk) or write oblique approval text (audit-quality risk).

Receipt digest churn: the runner re-attaches verification_execution_receipt_digest up to three times (after mutation flags, validation errors, and postflight_ref insertion, runner lines 521-539); any consumer or ledger that captures a digest before the final attach references a superseded value. Promotion tooling must consume only the final on-disk receipt.

Ledger is directory-of-JSON with no locking or produced append order; concurrent index-receipt runs can interleave, and until ledger_index emission lands, deletion or replacement of individual record files is only detectable via duplicate/chain-digest checks, not sequence gaps — weak footing for promotion evidence in adversarial settings.

Semantic overload of 'disabled' pins: plan/approval REQUIRED_DISABLED_AUTHORITY still assert subprocess_execution/direct_execution disabled and approval_scope pins future_execution_path='b1_3_runner_required' (verification_execution_approval.py lines 22-35, 296-304) even though the B1.3B runner does execute subprocesses; extending to B2 promotion gating without a schema-version story risks either false governance claims in artifacts or breaking every existing validator simultaneously.

CodeVault bridge naming collision: hitl_promotion_artifacts.py forbids active-state words including 'verified' in promotion artifacts (_FORBIDDEN_ACTIVE_STATES, line 45), so the CodeVault evidence tier must be named and validated carefully to avoid tripping platform-wide truth scanners while still conveying test-pass evidence.
